officialTitle: Perioperative Pembrolizumab for Early-Stage Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: 797 participants were randomly assigned to the pembrolizumab group (n=397) or the placebo group (n=400)
design.notes: Randomisation stratified by disease stage, PD-L1 expression, histology and region.

clinicalQuestion: Does perioperative pembrolizumab (neoadjuvant with cisplatin-based chemotherapy plus adjuvant) improve EFS and OS in resectable stage II–IIIB (N2) NSCLC?

pico.population: Resectable stage II, IIIA or IIIB (N2) NSCLC
pico.intervention: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks with cisplatin-based chemotherapy for four cycles, surgery, then adjuvant pembrolizumab for up to 13 cycles
pico.comparator: Neoadjuvant placebo plus cisplatin-based chemotherapy, surgery, then adjuvant placebo
pico.outcomes: Dual primary: EFS and OS. Secondary: MPR, pCR, safety

arms.label: Perioperative pembrolizumab
arms.regimen: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus cisplatin-based chemotherapy, surgery, adjuvant pembrolizumab
arms.dosing: Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks (4 neoadjuvant cycles with chemotherapy; up to 13 adjuvant cycles)
arms.doseSourceQuote: neoadjuvant pembrolizumab (200 mg) or placebo once every 3 weeks, each of which was given with cisplatin-based chemotherapy for 4 cycles, followed by surgery and adjuvant pembrolizumab (200 mg) or placebo once every 3 weeks for up to 13 cycles

arms.label: Placebo
arms.regimen: Neoadjuvant placebo plus cisplatin-based chemotherapy, surgery, adjuvant placebo

publications.title: Perioperative Pembrolizumab for Early-Stage Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: First interim analysis (EFS)

publications.title: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab compared with neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone in patients with early-stage non-small-cell lung cancer (KEYNOTE-671): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
publications.label: Second interim analysis (OS)

outcomes.sourceQuote: Event-free survival at 24 months was 62.4% in the pembrolizumab group and 40.6% in the placebo group (hazard ratio for progression, recurrence, or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.46 to 0.72; P<0.001).
The estimated 24-month overall survival was 80.9% in the pembrolizumab group and 77.6% in the placebo group (P = 0.02, which did not meet the significance criterion).

A major pathological response occurred in 30.2% of the participants in the pembrolizumab group and in 11.0% of those in the placebo group (difference, 19.2 percentage points; 95% CI, 13.9 to 24.7; P<0.0001; threshold, P = 0.0001)
a pathological complete response occurred in 18.1% and 4.0%, respectively (difference, 14.2 percentage points; 95% CI, 10.1 to 18.7; P<0.0001; threshold, P = 0.0001)

36-month overall survival estimates were 71% (95% CI 66-76) in the pembrolizumab group and 64% (58-69) in the placebo group (hazard ratio 0·72 [95% CI 0·56-0·93]; one-sided p=0·0052; threshold, one-sided p=0·0054).
Median event-free survival was 47·2 months (95% CI 32·9 to not reached) in the pembrolizumab group and 18·3 months (14·8-22·1) in the placebo group (hazard ratio 0·59 [95% CI 0·48-0·72]).

safety.description: Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events across all phases
safety.sourceQuote: Across all treatment phases, 44.9% of the participants in the pembrolizumab group and 37.3% of those in the placebo group had treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or higher, including 1.0% and 0.8%, respectively, who had grade 5 events.

strengths: OS as a dual primary endpoint, met at second interim analysis
limitations: Design cannot isolate the contribution of the adjuvant phase
Higher rate of grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events

clinicalImplications.text: Established perioperative pembrolizumab with cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy as a standard for resectable stage II–IIIB (N2) NSCLC, with a significant overall survival benefit.

tumourBoardPearl.text: KEYNOTE-671 is the perioperative trial with OS as a dual primary endpoint met — but it cannot tell you whether the adjuvant phase adds to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy alone.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstracts of PMIDs 37272513 (first interim) and 39288781 (second interim OS).
